nodes.label: Roadmap status
nodes.rationale: A sketch, not a contract — nothing in it is committed work; README names the current scope and CHANGELOG names what landed.

nodes.label: v0.16.0 — entry points, logging and old defects
nodes.rationale: The largest window so far at 181 commits, landing three things together plus a packaging-surface cleanup: no more dangling source maps (#1007), NodeNext resolution (#1008), and @types/node no longer a silent requirement for reading the public API (#1006).

nodes.label: Core-only root export (#414)
nodes.rationale: One barrel re-exporting every subsystem shipped the testkit in the production entry (#685) and made `import { ActorSystem }` pay for whatever any subsystem pulled in eagerly (#1005); eighteen subsystems now get their own entry, and the smoke suite loads every declared entry on all three runtimes.

nodes.label: Logging sink architecture (#1150)
nodes.rationale: The logger wrote to exactly one place; it now fans one record out to as many destinations as configured, each dependency-free, with nothing about the existing surface changed — a system whose config nobody edited logs exactly what it logged yesterday.

nodes.label: 50-oldest bug/security wave
nodes.rationale: 42 of the 50 oldest open defects resolved. Two of the fifty were not defects at all, five entries are BREAKING, and independent verification found five regressions the wave itself introduced — the worst being #588's own fix, where a new inbound-connection cap armed no handshake deadline, so 1024 silent sockets saturated it and refused every real peer: a defence that became the attack.

nodes.label: 50-oldest production-goal wave
nodes.rationale: Triage before code was the expensive half: every issue was read against today's tree asking 'are the acceptance criteria met' rather than 'does the defect still exist', and 277 claims in the issue bodies did not survive it. Unreachability is now deliberately NOT reconciled — on the no-lease path 'hosted somewhere' and 'at most one' cannot both be had, because reaching the incumbent to ask it to stand down is precisely what failed.

nodes.label: Wave 3 residuals (#1211–#1228)
nodes.rationale: Eighteen tracked residuals, each a defect the wave measured rather than inferred and deliberately did not fold in. Four of them are behaviour the wave shipped that no test binds — found by reverting one line at a time, not by reading — and they are the honest measure of what a green suite did not prove.

nodes.label: Gossip frame sequence field breaks rolling upgrades (#112)
nodes.rationale: GossipMessage gains a required sequence, so an upgraded peer refuses an old node's frames and an old node ignores the new one: membership does not converge in either direction while both versions run. The guard holds only while the sender is still a member — closing that residual needs #940's incarnation identity.

nodes.label: Feature-parity quick wins
nodes.rationale: Inbox for non-actor callers (#181), DeathWatch.watchWith (#159), and the ShardCommand types (#151).

nodes.label: Planned production features
nodes.rationale: Persistent reminders (#168), stateless workers (#170), saga / process-manager with compensations (#179) and placement strategies (#169).

nodes.label: Novel differentiators
nodes.rationale: Deterministic simulation testing with seeded virtual-time replay (#200), LLM agents as supervised durable actors (epic #421) and per-entity chaos injection (#206) — each gets its own plan slot.

nodes.label: Bigger threads (L/XL, own design phase)
nodes.rationale: A Streams DSL subset (#147) that is a deliberate ~5% subset rather than a replacement for the full Source/Flow/Sink composition DSL (#54), plus a WASM/edge subpackage (#209), distributed transactions (#171) and multi-DC clustering (#149).

nodes.label: Explicitly out of scope
nodes.rationale: Auto-magic cache invalidation by tag or pattern is a known bug-source, so invalidation stays explicit via cache.delete; and backwards-compatibility guarantees of any kind are out, because the project is pre-1.0.

nodes.label: Pull requests are not accepted
nodes.rationale: The issue tracker is the contribution channel: well-shaped issues are accepted, patches are not.

nodes.label: Comparison benchmarks against eight arms (#27)
nodes.rationale: benchmarks/comparison/ measures actor-ts against nact, XState, Akka and Pekko through both their Java and Scala APIs, Akka.NET and Orleans, publishing to the README, the bilingual reference/benchmarks pages and a generated RESULTS.md.
